reuse.why: The new range handler and existing consumers reuse recurConfigToRSchedule and the existing shared weekend-rule helpers.

duplication.why: Holiday matching, non-working-day detection, movement and daily skipping are shared rather than duplicated across consumers.

placement.why: Calendar rules remain in shared/schedules.ts, configuration belongs to the schedule model, and the new handler follows the existing server registration pattern.

scope.why: The changes are confined to the requested scheduling features, their consumers, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: The shared rule remains cohesive, although occurrence-count and range-padding calculations introduce separate bounds that maintainers must keep aligned with holiday semantics.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed consumers apply weekend and holiday decisions through applyWeekendRule or applyWeekendRuleToDay.

disguised_duplication.where: The diff extends the existing shared decision rather than recreating it under different names or shapes.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays, getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays argument, and applyWeekendRule gains the required daily-frequency branch; no consumers bypass the shared rule.
